title: Call: Fenwick Schools Nurse Coordinator — 29 Absent, Which Number?

caller.name: Margo Teller, RN
caller.label: Nurse Coordinator, Fenwick Community School District

transcript.speaker: District Nurse
transcript.text: Hi, this is Margo Teller at the district office. Attendance is in, and it's not good. We have 23 students and 6 staff out today, and every one of them is from a family that went to the supper Saturday.

transcript.speaker: District Nurse
transcript.text: Two of the staff are cafeteria workers at the middle school. One is an aide in our district preschool room. One of the cafeteria workers already called her manager. She says she feels better and wants to come back in tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: District Nurse
transcript.text: Dr. Anselm Voss is already drafting a letter to all families. He wants it out today. And he's asking me whether we should cancel Tuesday's homecoming game. I told him I'd ask you first.

transcript.speaker: District Nurse
transcript.text: I can send you the absentee list by student ID, with grade and building. No names unless you need them. But here's my real problem. I need to know what number goes in the letter. The hospital told one of our parents fourteen. Is it fourteen? Is it more? I don't want our letter saying one thing and yours saying another.

transcript.speaker: District Nurse
transcript.text: Oh, and about eleven percent of our families will need it in Spanish, and the district office says that's four hours from when they get the final text. So the sooner the better.

transcript.speaker: District Nurse
transcript.text: So... what number do I give him, what do I tell my two cafeteria workers and the preschool aide, and what do I tell him about the game? He's waiting on me.

voiceStyles.District Nurse: Woman in her 50s, experienced school nurse, calm but hurried, papers rustling, phone ringing in the background of a busy district office
voiceStyles.MCHD: Health department staff member, neutral, professional

instructorNote: This call tests whether the room keeps one count and one voice. Watch for three things. The Nurse Manager should set up exclusion counseling for the two cafeteria workers and the preschool aide, including the worker who wants to return Tuesday, and should add school cases to the interview priority list. The Epi Lead should accept the absentee list by student ID for case finding without adding the 29 absences to the count. The PIO should say the letter waits for MCHD-approved text with the single line-list count and its as-of time (17 coded cases, not the hospital's 14), plan time for the Spanish translation, and leave the homecoming decision with the superintendent until MCHD makes a recommendation (MCHD-COM-03 section 5).
